item.title: Putin-Trump-Xi: Three men, three different agendas
item.description: An unprecedented trilateral summit of the leaders of China, Russia and the US will provide startling images and unsettle Europe this week, but all three presidents are approaching the meeting with starkly different agendas. Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will meet Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen for talks that have echoes of the US-UK-USSR February 1945 “big three” summit in Yalta. At that meeting, which took place months before the end of World War II, the leaders of Britain, the Soviet Union and the US agreed the postwar division of Europe. Europe, which will not have a representative at Thursday’s talks, will be eyeing them warily. The smiles and friendly handshakes may also cause chills in Ukraine, after almost half a decade of war with Russia, and Taiwan, the democratic island viewed by China as part of its territory. But analysts say it is unlikely that the meeting will result in a landmark breakthrough on key issues such as Ukraine, nuclear disarmament and AI, even if the fact it is taking place at all is remarkable. Here AFP looks at what the three men will want from the meeting. Putin: imagery and Ukraine On paper, Putin will be in the meeting as the junior partner, presiding over a country whose population, let alone economy, is dwarfed by both the United States and China. But the war sparked by Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine, which Trump famously vowed to resolve in 24 hours, will be at the centre of the talks as the conflict grinds towards its fifth anniversary. Putin will be buoyed by being able to set out his conditions for ending the war without Kyiv’s chief allies, the Europeans, or Ukraine being at the table. “He wants Russia, the US and China to decide everyone else’s geopolitical fate. But in the end it’s impossible to decide on the fundamentals of European security without Europeans,” said Fredrik Wesslau, senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR). The optics of the meeting, set to be relayed extensively by Russia’s state-controlled media, are also very important for Putin who has always pressed for Moscow to be seen as a great global power even after the collapse of the USSR. “A seat alongside the American and Chinese presidents would affirm Russia’s status as a global power, despite its much weaker economic position,” said Tsiporah Fried, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute. “Political rehabilitation would be a gain even without concessions on territory, sanctions, or Ukraine’s future alignment,” she added. Trump: nuclear and overcoming midterms Trump and the White House have framed the trilateral summit as a way of advancing nuclear arms control, although the president himself admitted before leaving Washington “it’s a tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes.” The imagery is also important for Trump as the 80-year-old contemplates his last two years in office as a lame-duck president followin

item.title: Supreme Court reserves judgment in Zamfara North APC senatorial dispute
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Supreme Court on Wednesday reserved judgment in the legal dispute concerning the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for the Zamfara North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. A five-member panel of the court, led by Justice Tijani Abubakar, reserved the matter for judgment after the contending parties adopted their respective briefs of argument. The appeal, marked SC/CV/840/2026, was lodged before the apex court by Senator Sahabi Ya’u, who is seeking to set aside a verdict the Sokoto Division of the Court of Appeal delivered in the matter. The APC had declared that Senator Ya’u won a primary election it conducted in the senatorial district on May 19. However, dissatisfied with the outcome of the primary, a governorship aspirant of the party, Dr. Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, took the matter to court. While challenging the process that led to the emergence of Senator Ya’u as the party’s flag bearer, Shinkafi told the court that no valid primary was conducted in the senatorial district. Processes before the court showed that the party had cleared three aspirants, Hanafi Musa Moriki, Shinkafi and Ya’u, to contest the primary poll. Shinkafi, in his suit, maintained that, contrary to the APC’s position, no valid consensus was reached among the aspirants to warrant the nomination of Senator Ya’u as the unopposed candidate. He told the court that he neither withdrew nor endorsed anyone as a consensus nominee, adding that he did not submit any written consent to withdraw from the race. Cited as respondents in the matter were the APC, INEC and Senator Ya’u. Meanwhile, in a judgment delivered on August 31, Justice Hassan Dikko of the Federal High Court in Gusau, Zamfara State, nullified the primary poll and ordered the APC to conduct a fresh one within 14 days. The high court held that the action of the APC was not in tandem with the principle of internal democracy entrenched in the party’s Constitution. Dissatisfied with the judgment, Senator Ya’u lodged an appeal before the Sokoto Division of the Court of Appeal. He, among other things, challenged the jurisdiction of the high court to meddle in a matter he said was within the realm of the domestic affairs of a political party and therefore non-justiciable. However, the appeal was dismissed, as the appellate court upheld the high court’s decision in the matter. Not happy with the verdict, Senator Ya’u approached the Supreme Court to set aside the concurrent decisions of the two lower courts. While the appellant argued his case on Wednesday through a team of lawyers led by Mr. Wale Balogun, SAN, the 1st respondent, Dr. Shinkafi, was represented by Mr. Bello Galadi, who filed a brief of argument on November 13 urging the court to dismiss the appeal for want of merit. item.title: NLC, TUC end rift, unite against anti-worker policies
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Nigeria’s two major labour centres, the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), have resolved their differences and agreed to strengthen their cooperation following the intervention of former leaders of both organisations. The reconciliation, announced at a joint world press conference on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, marks an end to the public disagreement that had threatened unity within the organised labour movement. The peace deal was brokered by former presidents of the two labour centres, who intervened to resolve the dispute and restore harmonious working relations between their leaderships. In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and TUC President General, Comrade Festus Osifo, the organisations reaffirmed their commitment to unity, solidarity and the protection of Nigerian workers’ rights and welfare. The statement acknowledged that a misunderstanding between the two labour centres had played out in the public domain but said the intervention of their former leaders had successfully resolved the disagreement. “It is no longer news that a family misunderstanding arose between the two Labour Centers, which unfortunately played out in the public domain. However, in the true spirit of labour solidarity, maturity and collective responsibility, distinguished former presidents of NLC and TUC intervened and worked tirelessly to resolve the disagreements. “We are pleased to announce that their intervention has yielded the desired results, and the misunderstanding has been amicably resolved,” the statement said. The two organisations declared that the unity of Nigerian workers was more important than disagreements among their leaders, pledging to work together in the interest of workers, pensioners and other vulnerable groups. They said the challenges confronting Nigerian workers required solidarity rather than division, adding that their common struggle must not be undermined by institutional differences or leadership disagreements. Both centres also reaffirmed that workers’ welfare, dignity and material well-being remained non-negotiable, stressing that their renewed partnership would focus on confronting exploitation, defending decent work, demanding economic justice and resisting policies they consider detrimental to workers and pensioners. “We are determined to ensure that our differences do not provide an opportunity for anti-worker forces to weaken the labour movement or undermine the gains achieved through decades of collective struggle,” they said. To sustain the reconciliation, the labour centres said they had agreed to introduce measures to promote mutual respect, strengthen working relations, establish effective mechanisms for resolving future disagreements and prevent a recurrence of such disputes. item.title: JAMB ends office visits for course changes
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has introduced a fully online process for candidates seeking to change their preferred institutions or courses, eliminating the need for physical visits to its offices to access the service. The new arrangement allows candidates to independently make the changes through the Board’s e-Facility portal from any location with internet access. The initiative is expected to reduce queues, transportation costs, waiting time and other inconveniences associated with physically accessing the service. In a statement issued by its Acting Director, Public Affairs and Protocol, Dr Fabian Benjamin, the Board said the development was part of efforts to improve service delivery and align its operations with the Federal Government’s Ease of Doing Business policy. Under the arrangement, candidates can complete the entire process, including payment, authentication and submission, online without visiting JAMB offices or accredited facilities. To access the service, candidates are required to log into the JAMB e-Facility portal at https://efacility.jamb.gov.ng using their registered email addresses and passwords. After logging in, they should select “Corrections and Uploads” from the sidebar menu, click on “Change of Programme/Institution”, select UTME and indicate the examination year for which the correction is required. Candidates are then expected to generate a payment invoice by clicking on “Make New Payment” and complete the transaction through the CREDO payment platform using a debit card or bank transfer. The Board advised candidates to return to the payment page on their profiles after making payment to confirm that the status has changed from “PENDING” to “PAID (Not Used)”. After confirming payment, candidates should return to the Change of Institution/Course page, enter their preferred institution and/or programme details and validate the transaction using a One-Time Password (OTP) sent to their registered email addresses. The process is completed by clicking the “SAVE” button, after which a confirmation message indicating that the change has been successfully made will be displayed. Candidates are also required to print their Change of Programme/Institution slips and log into the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) to confirm that their new choices have been updated. JAMB cautioned candidates to carefully review their selections before submitting requests to avoid errors. It also stressed that candidates must ensure their payment status reads “PAID (Not Used)” before proceeding and have access to their registered email accounts to receive and validate the OTP. The Board further advised candidates to carry out the process through their individual profiles rather than engage intermediaries or disclose their login details and OTPs to third parties. item.title: US Congress neither met nor endorsed Obi – Atiku’s lobbyists
item.description: A Washington-based lobbying firm hired by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Von Batten-Montague-York, has dismissed reports that the United States Congress met with or endorsed the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi. The firm said the event attended by Obi during his visit to Washington, DC, was a private gathering and did not constitute an official meeting with the US Congress. The clarification followed reports suggesting that Obi had secured the endorsement of members of the US Congress for his 2027 presidential ambition. Obi had announced on his X platform that he arrived in Washington, DC, on Monday, November 16, for a series of meetings and engagements with congressional leaders from both the House of Representatives and the Senate, as well as other influential American figures. He said the discussions focused on Nigeria’s development, security, economic prosperity and the future of the country’s democracy. However, Von Batten-Montague-York, in a statement posted on its X platform on Tuesday, said neither the Congress nor its relevant foreign affairs committee met with or endorsed Obi. The firm’s principal, Dr Von Batten, said he was responding to media reports claiming that Obi had received congressional endorsement, particularly after his firm was mentioned in a public commentary. He said, “Congress did not meet with or endorse Mr. Obi. The event he attended was private, and no one in the video is a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee or its Subcommittee on Africa, which oversees U.S. foreign policy toward Africa. “I know everyone in the video, and no official from the State Department’s Bureau of African Affairs appears in it either.” Batten said he recognised Congressman Marlin Stutzman and Congresswoman Beth Van Duyne, who were among the American figures Obi identified as having met during his visit. He, however, noted that neither lawmaker served on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, adding that they served on committees responsible for budget and small business matters. He said his clarification was not intended to diminish the significance of Obi’s visit but to correct what he described as inaccurate reports. In his earlier account of the visit, Obi said he held a substantive interview with American television commentator Glenn Beck, during which they discussed Nigeria’s challenges, accountable leadership and the management of the country’s resources. He also listed Stutzman, Van Duyne, former Congressman Todd Tiahrt, Suzanne Bock Grisham and retired US Army Colonel Albert V. Short among the people he met. Obi further said he addressed an audience on Capitol Hill, where he highlighted the need for international cooperation and support for Nigeria, particularly in security, national unity, economic development and democratic governance. item.title: Army intercepts 300 rounds of ammunition concealed in beans sack
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Troops of the Nigerian Army have arrested a 47-year-old man suspected of transporting ammunition to individuals in Kogi State, recovering 300 rounds of 7.62mm by 39mm ammunition concealed in a sack of beans. The interception followed an intelligence-led operation aimed at disrupting the supply of weapons and ammunition to criminal groups. The Army said the suspect, identified as Umaru Muhammad, a resident of Ashe Village, was intercepted at about 9:30pm on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, by troops of the Atsawa Blocking Force working with local vigilantes. In a statement on Wednesday, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said a search of the suspect’s belongings led to the discovery of the ammunition concealed in the sack of beans. According to the statement, preliminary interrogation indicated that the ammunition was allegedly intended for two individuals identified as Gimba and Dare, reportedly residents of Gori Village along the River Niger corridor in Lokoja Local Government Area of Kogi State. The Army said the identities and alleged roles of the individuals were being investigated, adding that the circumstances surrounding the attempted transfer of the ammunition remained subject to further inquiries. Other items recovered from the suspect included a Bajaj motorcycle, a mobile telephone and ₦30,500 in cash. Muhammad is currently in military custody as investigations continue to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged ammunition transaction and identify other persons who may be connected to it. The Army said the operation formed part of its ongoing efforts to disrupt the supply of arms, ammunition and other logistics to groups involved in terrorism, banditry and kidnapping. It added that troops would sustain intelligence-driven operations and strengthen cooperation with local security stakeholders to prevent criminal activities. The Army also urged members of the public to report suspicious movements, particularly the transportation of concealed arms, ammunition and other prohibited items, to security agencies. It reaffirmed its commitment to protecting communities and supporting efforts to restore peace and security across the country. The post Army intercepts 300 rounds of ammunition concealed in beans sack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Arewa group faults northern elders over Tinubu criticism
item.description: … Calls for broader consultation before claiming to speak for North By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — The Arewa Emerging Elites Round Table has disagreed with recent comments by Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, Dr Usman Bugaje, former Minister Adamu Maina Waziri and Prof Usman Yusuf on President Bola Tinubu’s administration, insisting that the views of a few individuals should not be presented as the collective position of Northern Nigeria. The group made its position known at a press conference in Kaduna, where it called for broader consultation among stakeholders before anyone claims to speak on behalf of the region. Reading a briefing titled, “Stop Hiding Naked Partisanship Behind the Sacred Robes of Arewa Eldership: You Do Not Speak for the North!”, the group’s chairman, Abubakar A. Kurawa, said Northern Nigeria comprised diverse interests and perspectives that should be adequately represented in public discussions. The organisation expressed concern over what it described as attempts to interpret comments made at a book presentation in Abuja as reflecting the position of the 19 Northern states. It questioned whether traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth organisations, professional groups and ordinary citizens across the region had been adequately consulted before such positions were presented as representing the North. The group maintained that individuals had the constitutional right to criticise government policies and express concerns about the administration but argued that such opinions should be clearly distinguished from the collective position of the region. It said public discussions about the performance of the Federal Government should accommodate different perspectives rather than suggest that a particular gathering or group of individuals represented the views of all Northern Nigerians. The Round Table also called on political leaders and former public office holders from the region to demonstrate accountability by highlighting their contributions to the development of Northern Nigeria. It stressed that discussions about leadership and governance should focus on measurable contributions to addressing the challenges confronting the region. The organisation further urged Northern stakeholders to give greater attention to insecurity, agriculture, infrastructure, education and economic development, describing them as critical issues requiring sustained engagement with governments at all levels. It said political and developmental interests of the North should take precedence over individual political interests and called for constructive engagement with the Federal Government on issues affecting the region. The group also emphasised that criticism of government policies remained an important feature of democratic governance, adding that public officials should be open to scrutiny and accountability. item.title: Plateau killings: Obi condemns attacks, questions intelligence failures
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has mourned victims of the latest attacks in Plateau State, condemned the recurring killings in the state and questioned intelligence failures that have left communities vulnerable. In a statement posted on his X handle on Wednesday, Obi called for stronger security measures, thorough investigations and justice for the victims, saying the continued loss of lives showed the need for urgent action to protect Nigerians. “I am deeply saddened and troubled by reports that at least nine people were killed in the Zuwagal community, Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State, in yet another assault on innocent Nigerians,” Obi said. He described the killings as part of a “deeply concerning pattern of recurring attacks, displacement and the destruction of communities throughout the country.” Citing OpenWatch security incident records, Obi said 261 deaths were reported across Nigeria between November 2 and 15, including 24 in Plateau during the first week and 15 in the second. He added that Plateau recorded further attacks on November 16. “These victims are not merely numbers. They were fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners whose lives were abruptly ended, leaving families and entire communities to mourn,” he said, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and the people of Plateau State. Obi questioned why communities continued to face threats without adequate protection and why intelligence reports were not leading to preventive action. He called on the government and security agencies to reinforce operations in vulnerable communities, investigate the attacks, establish reliable early-warning and rapid-response systems, support displaced families and ensure those responsible were brought to justice. “Every Nigerian life is valuable, regardless of ethnicity, religion or political affiliation. The right to life must never be subject to negotiation,” he said. “Nigeria must do more than mourn those who have died. We must protect those who are still living.” Vanguard reported that at least five people were killed in fresh attacks on communities in Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi local government areas. The latest incident occurred at about 9pm on Sunday, November 15, when suspected terrorists attacked Zwagal community in Jipal District, Mangu, killing three people, while others were reported missing. Two other people were killed in separate attacks in Riyom and Barkin Ladi. The Berom Youth Moulders Association said Da Ishaku Pam Vwos, 79, was killed in Sho village, Barkin Ladi, and Dauda John Davou, 42, was killed in Sambak community, Riyom. The association also said attackers entered Jol community but met resistance from local vigilantes. item.title: Subsidy benefits went to intermediaries, not Nigerians — Uzodimma
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, has said the benefits of Nigeria’s petroleum subsidy regime largely accrued to intermediaries in the oil sector rather than ordinary Nigerians it was designed to protect. Uzodimma stated this on Wednesday while delivering an address at the ongoing 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. The forum was organised by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and hosted by the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR). The governor said responsible governance required building public trust through community engagement, stakeholder relations and inclusive development. He described one of the greatest tests of leadership as taking difficult decisions that initially hurt the people but are expected to benefit them in the long run, while maintaining honest communication to secure public understanding and trust. He said: “I like to think about leadership, the experience I learned in leading Imo State as governor and keeping the trust. Especially when you want to accept a decision that will hurt people first before such decisions will help them. “It is even tougher when the administration is new and when the people are yet to see tangible results they can relate to.” Citing the removal of the petroleum subsidy as an example, Uzodimma said the policy was originally intended to ease the burden on ordinary Nigerians but that much of its benefits went to intermediaries in the petroleum sector. “The petroleum subsidy was meant to help ordinary Nigerians. But most of the benefits ended up with intermediaries in the sector,” he said. He defended President Bola Tinubu’s decision to remove the subsidy, describing it as necessary in the overall interest of the country. According to him, Nigerians across different sectors and segments of society had openly called for the removal of the subsidy before the policy was implemented. “Do not forget that before he did that, Nigerians across different sectors and segments had openly canvassed and demanded that it be removed,” he said. The governor further argued that the removal had increased the resources available to state governments and the Federal Capital Territory for infrastructure and socioeconomic development. He, however, acknowledged that the resulting price adjustments had created difficulties for many households, stressing that reforms were more likely to deliver their intended benefits when citizens understood the reasons behind them. Using an example from Imo State, Uzodimma explained how government interventions could benefit some groups while initially affecting the livelihoods of others. item.title: Super Eagles move up to 29th in latest FIFA world rankings
item.description: The Nigerian Super Eagles have moved up one place to 29th in the latest FIFA men’s world rankings released on Wednesday. The improvement also sees the team climb to fifth position among African countries, overtaking Algeria, which dropped out of the continent’s top five. The Super Eagles’ latest progress comes after their two November fixtures against Tanzania in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Eric Chelle’s men began the international window with a 3-1 victory over the Taifa Stars at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo last Friday. However, Nigeria failed to maintain their winning run, settling for a goalless draw against the same opponents in Tuesday’s return fixture at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar. Morocco retained their position as Africa’s highest-ranked team, followed by Senegal, Egypt and Côte d’Ivoire in second, third and fourth places, respectively. On the global ranking, Spain maintained their position as the world’s number one team, while Argentina, France and England retained their places among the top five. item.title: NLC, TUC Resolve Disagreement After N70,000 Transport Allowance Controversy
item.description: The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have resolved their recent disagreement, following the recent banter over the N70,000 one-off six-month allowance approved by President Tinubu. The two labour centres announced the resolution of the dispute on Wednesday at a joint press conference held in Abuja. In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and TUC President-General, Festus Osifo, the unions acknowledged that their disagreement had played out publicly but insisted that their shared history and responsibility to Nigerian workers must take precedence over leadership and institutional differences. Reaffirming their commitment to a united labour movement and the collective defence of workers’ rights, they described the disagreement as a family misunderstanding that had now been amicably settled through the intervention of former leaders of both organisations. A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The controversy followed its approval by the Federal Government for workers across all levels for six months. While speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief recently, Comrade Joe Ajero argued that the Union has the power to negotiate alone on labour matters based on the principle of most workers representatives of the International Labour Organization (ILO). “TUC can negotiate along with NLC, but NLC can negotiate alone based on the principle of most workers representatives of the ILO”, the NLC President noted. On his part, the TUC President, while also appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief , described the N70,000 agreement by the NLC President as an aberration, saying that the TUC was not carried along in the negotiations. Osifo challenged Ajaero to produce the ILO regulation document that said either of the labour unions could negotiate on behalf of the other. “He should show me in the ILO Regulations where it says one party is going to negotiate without the other one being there or consulted. He should show me! He should show Nigerians! NLC determines how TUC participates”, Ajaero adding that the TUC does not submit its proposal to TUC. “It is the other way round,” he stated that the Ministry of Labour and other labour authorities will not engage with the Trade Union, as it acts alone on workers’ welfare negotiations. The trade congress leader, in his reply, said, “As I listened to Ajaero today, I was wondering if it is the same NLC that produced the likes of Adams Oshiomole, Hassan Sumonu, Ayuba Wabba and so on. “There is nowhere in ILO regulations that says a trade centre cannot negotiate for its members. It is not there! It is just that if you are going to the ILO, it is tripartite- the labour, government and the employers. item.title: ‘Fake Agency’ Case: Adeyemi in custody for his own safety, ICPC tells court
item.description: … as defendants plead not guilty, beg for bail By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) said on Wednesday that it kept the self-styled Director-General (DG) of the alleged “non-existent” Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Prince Adeniyi Adeyemi, in custody for his own safety. According to the Commission, many of those allegedly defrauded by the defendant, a number of whom have filed petitions against him, are capable of physically harming him on sight. It therefore prayed the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), sitting at Maitama in Abuja, to reject an application that Adeyemi filed to be released on bail pending the determination of the criminal charge against him. “My lord, the defendant is facing allegations of obtaining by false pretence. “There are many petitions against him, and the people who lodged those petitions are after him. “There is this particular man from Ibadan whom he defrauded, which formed part of the counts in the charge. He has been seriously searching for him. “We believe that it will be in his own best interest to remain in custody for safekeeping,” the prosecution counsel, Mr. Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, added. The ICPC urged the court to also deny bail to four civil servants who are facing trial alongside the alleged fake PFIPC DG. The anti-corruption agency took the position after the defendants pleaded not guilty to a 36-count amended charge it entered against them. All the defendants, through their respective lawyers, begged the court to release them on bail pending the determination of the charge. They anchored their bail applications on the provisions of sections 35(4) and 36(5) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, as well as sections 158 and 162 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015. The civil servants who were docked alongside Adeyemi on Wednesday are Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe. All the defendants, including Adeyemi, pleaded ill health, even as they pledged to make themselves available for trial. However, the prosecution counsel urged the court to refuse their bail requests and order an accelerated hearing of the case. The ICPC specifically alleged that Adeyemi posed a flight risk, insisting he had enough funds at his disposal and the capacity to influence some of the proposed witnesses in the matter. Meanwhile, in urging the court to grant him bail on very liberal terms, Adeyemi, through his counsel, Mr. Ibrahim Angulu, SAN, told the court that, contrary to the prosecution’s claim, all his bank accounts had been frozen. “My lord, the accounts of the defendant were frozen, including those of his wives. item.title: Nigeria still yearns for visionary leaders like Nnamdi Azikiwe – Abaribe
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – Senator Enyinnaya Abaribe representing Abia South Senator District, has praised the leadership philosophy of Nigeria’s first President, the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, lamenting that the country is still struggling to find leaders capable of providing the kind of purposeful leadership championed by the late nationalist He stated that Azikiwe demonstrated exemplary leadership through his emphasis on education, social reorientation, freedom, infrastructural development and visionary thinking, which he used as instruments for shaping society and advancing national development. Senator Abaribe who made the remarks during the 14th edition of the Zik Lecture Series held under the theme, “Zik’s Vision for Renaissance: Lessons from Emerging Economies in Africa”, identified himself as a student of Zik’s leadership philosophy, noting that the late statesman represented a generation of leaders whose political influence was guided by clear principles and a strong commitment to societal transformation. According to Abaribe, “leadership, as demonstrated by Azikiwe, went beyond the acquisition of political power to include the effective use of available resources and opportunities to influence the direction of a people”. He expressed concern that several African countries, particularly Nigeria, had continued to search for leaders committed to the principles of purposeful governance long after Azikiwe’s departure. Highlighting some of the challenges confronting Nigeria, the lawmaker identified weaknesses in the education sector, the growing divide between moral and immoral values, uncontrolled exposure to social media and the breakdown of family structures as issues requiring urgent attention. He, however, expressed optimism that recognising and acknowledging these problems would constitute an important step towards finding lasting solutions. Abaribe explained that his intention was not necessarily to provide immediate solutions but to draw attention to the deep-rooted challenges confronting the country and the African continent. He urged Nigerians to reflect deeply on the situation and take deliberate steps towards breaking the cycle of societal problems. Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Prof. Okechukwu Bond Anyiehie, described the theme of the lecture as timely and relevant to the country’s quest for development. Anyaehie noted that universities should not be seen merely as institutions for awarding academic degrees but as centres for generating ideas capable of driving societal transformation. Addressing the graduating students, whom he fondly referred to as Great Zikites, the Vice-Chancellor urged them to carry forward the ideals of courage, intellectual excellence, scholarship and Pan-Africanism associated with the late Azikiwe. item.title: EU proposes new 45bn euro Ukraine loan
item.description: The European Union on Wednesday proposed member states give Ukraine an extra 45-billion-euro ($49 billion) loan to plug Kyiv’s 2027 budget shortfalls as Russia’s war drags on. The funding would go two-thirds of the way towards filling a 70-billion-euro black hole Kyiv is facing next year — with Brussels looking to incentivise other Ukraine backers to do the rest. “Five years since the start of this war of aggression, Europe stands united. We are as committed as ever to support Ukraine in war and in peace,” European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said. “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiation table, and Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.” EU leaders will discuss the loan at a summit in Brussels next week in the hope of reaching a deal. The EU is currently paying out a 90-billion-loan to Kyiv that it hoped would see the country through to the end of next year. But as Russia has intensified its attacks it has become clear that those funds would not be enough. The new loan would follow the same format as the current one and be borrowed against headroom in the EU’s central budget. It would also be linked to Kyiv pressing on with reforms. While the aim is to forge agreement next week, the issue of the funding has now become wrapped up with broader fraught negotiations over the EU’s next central budget. Budget brawl German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has insisted that all of the EU must settle the financing and all 27 member states must be involved before a deal can be reached on the budget. That has rankled several of the EU’s least pro-Ukraine countries who want to be left out of backing the loan, such as Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Slovakia. Last time round, Budapest, Bratislava and Prague managed to get themselves exempted from having to help cover the financing. Von der Leyen insisted the aim this time remains to get all countries on board. Beyond the bloc, Brussels is pushing other allies of Ukraine – such as Britain, Canada and Japan to fill in the rest of Kyiv’s needs next year. Similar pleas have previously fallen short. In a bid to incentivise them this time, Brussels says others could provide guarantees to help bolster the loan or use the interest on frozen Russian assets in the EU to cover their own financing. The proposal for a new loan means that the EU for now won’t try to look into the thorny issue of directly tapping over 200 billion euros of frozen Russian central bank assets held in the bloc to fund Ukraine. That plan was shot down in 2025 by Belgium — where the majority of the assets are held — and the position of its government has not shifted. item.title: Nigerian Artist Wins Global Super Group ‘Art of the Game’ Competition, Securing £10,000 Donation for Lagos Charity
item.description: Super Group, the parent company of leading sportsbook brand Betway, has announced Nigerian artist Omomurewa Alade as the winner of its global Art of the Game competition. In recognition of her creative achievement, Alade received a £10,000 cash prize, while an additional £10,000 was donated to her chosen charity, the Feed the Widows Project in Lagos. Launched by Super Group earlier this year, Art of the Game invited artists from around the world to create a custom basketball design inspired by their culture, identity and personal creative vision. The competition was designed to celebrate the connection between sport, art and community, while creating a lasting impact beyond the competition itself. Alade’s winning design stood out among entries submitted from across the globe, impressing judges with its creativity, originality and representation of cultural identity. As part of her prize, Alade received £10,000, while a further £10,000 donation was awarded to Feed the Widows Project, a Lagos-based organisation dedicated to supporting widows and vulnerable members of the community. The donation forms part of Super Group Cares, the company’s global social impact programme focused on empowering communities and creating meaningful opportunities around the world. Kirsty Ross, Chief Operating Officer at Super Group, commented: “Art of the Game was created to celebrate the powerful connection between sport, creativity and community. Omomurewa Alade’s design captured that spirit brilliantly, and we’re delighted that her success will also make a meaningful difference through Feed the Widows Project. Through Super Group Cares, we remain committed to supporting initiatives that create lasting impact in the communities where we operate.” Representatives from Feed the Widows Project welcomed the donation, highlighting the positive impact it will have on the organisation’s ongoing programmes and outreach efforts. Since launching earlier this year, Art of the Game has showcased the creativity and diversity of artists from around the world, demonstrating how sport can inspire artistic expression while helping to deliver meaningful community impact. item.title: Iran, allies hit Gulf countries after US attack on island
item.description: Gulf nations scrambled to intercept incoming fire on Wednesday, after Iran and its allies lashed out following a US strike on a strategic island, in attacks that threatened to derail efforts to end the war. Kuwait activated its air defences to counter drone strikes – the first since early September – and Bahrain said it fended off an Iranian attack, after the United States struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the flashpoint Strait of Hormuz. Explosions were heard in Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude oil exporter, which said it intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Iran-backed Houthis, who have been seizing fresh territory in neighbouring Yemen. Bahrain has now suffered four Iranian attacks in six days, ending a weeks-long respite in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic on February 28. Iran responded by striking America’s wealthy Gulf allies, which host US military bases, and blockading Hormuz, which before the war carried a quarter of global oil flows. The Iranian army said “combat and kamikaze drones” targeted US air defence systems and launch platforms at Kuwait’s Ali Al-Salem air base on Wednesday. A day earlier, American fighter jets hit a missile launch site on Qeshm Island with “precision munitions”, a US military official said, describing it as a riposte to Iranian aggression. ‘Dangerous escalation’ Iran’s army chief Amir Hatami warned of a “more devastating” reaction to America and its allies. “Should the enemy make a mistake and repeat actions that have previously led them to despair, our response — directed at both the enemy and their backers — will undoubtedly be even more devastating and will know no geographical boundaries,” Hatami said, according to Iran’s Fars news agency. Mediator Qatar, which held talks with Iranian officials on Tuesday, called the latest attacks a “dangerous escalation” and warned they undercut efforts to find a peaceful solution. “The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that could complicate efforts to contain tensions and undermine political and diplomatic efforts aimed at ensuring the security and stability of the region,” a foreign ministry statement said. Kuwaiti residents described feelings of foreboding as attacks returned to the tiny, oil-rich country, which was hit hard by Iranian strikes earlier in the war. “The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying,” said Egyptian resident Hani Mohammed, 40. “People had started to readjust to a normal life. The sounds of planes and explosions no longer set the pace of daily life as before. But what happened has revived feelings of anxiety.” Windows rattled Meanwhile, one seafarer was missing after a ship belonging to ADNOC, the United Arab Emirates’ oil giant, was struck late on Tuesday in Hormuz, the company said. item.title: Benue North East: Court declares Suswam as APC valid senatorial candidate
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday declared former Governor of Benue, Gabriel Suswam, as the valid candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 Benue North East senatorial election. Justice Inyang Ekwo, in a judgment, agreed with the argument of the ex-governor that he was unlawfully substituted by the party, having won the majority of the valid votes cast. Justice Ekwo held that the substitution was not in synch with the provisions of the Electoral Act and the 1999 Constitution (as amended), including the APC’s Constitution. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suswam had, in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1470/2026, prayed the court to recognise him as the validly elected candidate of the APC for the senatorial district. The former governor joined the APC, incumbent Sen. Emmanuel Udenbe and INEC as defendants in the suit. At the last proceedings, counsel to INEC, Anthony Malik, SAN, told the court that documents relating to the conduct of the primary indicated that Suswam won the exercise. Malik urged the court to determine the dispute in accordance with the result of the primary election, maintaining that the electoral body had placed before the court its report on the exercise, as well as the result. He consequently asked the court to uphold the outcome showing Suswam as the winner of the primary. Suswam’s counsel, Jibrin Okutepa, SAN, also urged the court to grant the reliefs sought by his client. Okutepa asked the court to reject the preliminary objections raised against the suit by the APC and Udenbe, arguing that the objections lacked merit. However, counsel to the APC, A. G. Yirvoms, asked the court to uphold the party’s preliminary objection and dismiss Suswam’s case. Suswam is challenging the decision of the APC to hand its Benue North East senatorial ticket to Udenbe despite his claim that he won the party’s primary election. item.title: China’s Xi greets Trump on arrival at Shenzhen airport
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping personally greeted Donald Trump at the airport as the US leader arrived Wednesday ahead of a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen that will also include Russia’s Vladimir Putin, AFP footage showed. After descending from Air Force One, Trump saluted as he stood alongside Xi on a red carpet lined with people waving colourful pom-poms and brandishing Chinese and American national flags, before the two leaders shook hands. Putin on war sanctions Meanwhile, President Vladimir Putin called Western sanctions on Russia a failure on Wednesday and met with his counterpart Xi Jinping in China ahead of their historic summit with US leader Donald Trump. Thursday’s trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could make decisions on the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence. Washington had signalled that Ukraine – something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem – was not expected to be addressed, before Trump said that it would. Putin, who met with Xi on Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen, was defiant on his war in Ukraine ahead of the three-man summit as he slammed Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion. “We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced an unprecedented sanctions pressure,” Putin said. After meeting the Russian leader, Xi urged closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should “leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties”. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said that sanctions on Russia “are going to continue to increase as long as this (Ukraine) war goes on.” Also up for discussion in Thursday’s trilateral meeting are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. item.title: UK-based Nigerian pastor jailed nearly 12 years for rape
item.description: A Nigerian church leader based in the United Kingdom, Brein Ayeni, has been sentenced to 11 years and nine months in prison for repeatedly raping a woman and subjecting her to coercive and controlling behaviour. West Midlands Police disclosed this in a statement on Monday , saying Ayeni, 43, was convicted of three counts of rape and one count of coercive or controlling behaviour following a trial. The offences were committed from June 2025, while Ayeni was head of Christworld Nation Church in Coventry, where he was regarded as a trusted figure in the community. The police said he recorded some of the attacks on his mobile phone and threatened to circulate the videos if the victim reported him, claiming they would show that the encounters were consensual. According to the statement, Ayeni also made derogatory remarks about the woman’s previous lifestyle and exhibited controlling behaviour after gaining her trust. The victim reported the abuse to the police in March 2026, prompting an investigation by specialist officers from the force’s Rape and Serious Sexual Offences team. Ayeni, who lived on Hurst Road, Coventry, was sentenced at Warwick Crown Court on Tuesday, November 10. In her victim impact statement, the woman said Ayeni’s position in the church had made her trust him, adding that the abuse had severely affected her mental and emotional well-being. “The title he held made me trust him, and that trust has been deeply damaged. The impact on my mental and emotional health is that I do not feel like the same person I was before all of this happened,” she said. She also described how the experience had affected her ability to trust others and maintain close relationships. “I struggle to trust people and allow them to get close to me because I am frightened of being taken advantage of again,” she said. The victim said reporting the abuse had required considerable courage because of the fear of being judged or disbelieved. Detective Sergeant Evie Griffiths, of the police force’s public protection unit, described the offences as horrific, noting that they had left the victim with lasting trauma. “These were horrific crimes which have understandably had a lasting impact. It is through her bravery in telling us what happened we were able to arrest Ayeni and stop him committing any further offences,” Griffiths said. She added that Ayeni had abused the trust placed in him to commit the offences and had been appropriately sentenced. The police also encouraged victims of rape and other sexual offences to seek support, whether or not they were ready to make a formal report. item.title: Two Clocks, One Election
item.description: The government wants economic improvement to reach voters. The opposition wants negotiations to produce cooperation. Both are running against time. Two clocks are ticking towards Nigeria’s presidential election. One measures how quickly economic improvement becomes visible in people’s lives. The other measures how quickly opposition leaders can turn discussions into an arrangement that strengthens their challenge. This week has brought movement on both. Figures released on Monday put October’s annual headline inflation at 14.06 per cent, down from 14.63 per cent in September. Meanwhile, opposition parties have announced a November 23 summit in Abuja to adopt cooperation documents. These developments give the governing party and its challengers something concrete to discuss. Neither, by itself, settles the electoral argument. For President Bola Tinubu, the task is to demonstrate that reform is improving living standards. For the opposition, it is to demonstrate that cooperation can survive competing ambitions. Inflation Falls. The Household Test Remains. The latest inflation figures offer the government evidence for its argument that economic stabilisation is progressing. Food inflation also moderated, to 19.13 per cent year on year from 19.59 per cent. The political meaning requires care. A lower annual inflation rate means prices are rising more slowly than a year earlier. It does not mean that the general price level has returned to where it stood before the cost of living shock. Families judge affordability through income, food, transport, rent and other recurring expenses. A household can recognise an improving economic indicator while remaining under considerable pressure. The government therefore has an opening, accompanied by a demanding question: how much improvement will citizens experience before they vote? Its strongest argument would connect stabilisation with changes people can identify: more reliable services, stronger earnings, affordable essentials and business opportunities. The opposition also needs to respond seriously to improving data. It can question the distribution and adequacy of recovery while explaining how its own policies would improve purchasing power. The emerging debate should concern the route from economic stability to household security. November 23: Cooperation Acquires a Date The Coalition for Democracy says participating opposition parties will meet at the NAF Conference Centre in Abuja on Monday, November 23. The proposed business includes a National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, a Framework for Opposition Unity and a National Reform Programme. That is a clearer next step than another general declaration of willingness to work together. But several forms of cooperation remain possible. Parties can coordinate election monitoring, defend campaign freedoms and agree on institutional reforms while continuing to field competing presidential candidates.
